board.note: Nothing was ticked and nothing was rejected on the last board, so I have taken it as a page you did not open and kept its three sharpest lines for a second and final showing. The four new ones test something narrower than “one shape”. Look at what has actually survived: Hamming on research, Cherny on building, Karpathy on demos, Han Kang on writing — every one of them is a person describing the work they do with their own hands. What has failed is everyone standing outside it: Hirschman, Simon, Meadows, O'Neill, the Vatican. Not theorists of systems, then, but practitioners on their own craft. So: a mathematician on what rigour is for, a surgeon on the difference between not knowing and not doing, a novelist on why an event is not an experience, and an opposition leader on what the refrigerators were actually for. I dropped Paul Graham's How to Do Great Work, which had two lines that passed — it is the same register you already mine yourself every week, and finding you what you would find anyway is not my job.
